commodity_commentary: The two-week commodity tape was dominated by the Strait of Hormuz crisis and its resolution — WTI crude swung from US$80.56 to a peak near US$128/bbl before collapsing to US$83.85 on the April 17 reopening, while Brent followed a parallel path from its 52-week high of US$118.35 down to US$90.38141540. Precious metals advanced on safe-haven flows, with gold reaching US$4,816/oz on April 16 — a new intra-period high — and silver climbing above US$80/oz1722. Base metals tracked China's Q1 GDP beat of 5.0% and March import surge of +27.8%, with copper gaining 3.32% to US$6.07/lb and nickel rising 4.81% month-over-month to US$17,985/tonne192132. Henry Hub natural gas fell to US$2.67/MMBtu, a 17-month low, on elevated storage and mild demand18. Agriculture was mixed: wheat advanced 4.7% on global supply concerns while the Nutrien potash proxy declined 3.56%48. The Lagging Indicator cross-reference engine links the period's commodity moves to 364 mining projects ($159.5B) and 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) tracked in the database, plus 785 power and energy projects with input-cost exposure to energy prices1417.

wcs_analysis.narrative: The WCS discount widened to US$16.25/bbl below WTI on April 13, up from US$15.55 on April 11. With the Strait of Hormuz reopening on April 17 sending WTI to US$83.85, the implied WCS level dropped to approximately US$67.60 (US$83.85 minus US$16.25), which if sustained would compress netbacks for heavy crude producers and place additional pressure on the 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) tracked in the database.

commodities.name: WTI Crude Oil
commodities.commentary: WTI Crude Oil: US$83.85/bbl (-11.4% on the April 17 session) — WTI recorded the most volatile two-week period in recent oil market history, ranging from US$80.56 to US$117.63 between March 18 and April 18 as the Strait of Hormuz crisis disrupted 20% of global oil supplies1438. The IEA characterized the closure as the largest supply disruption on record37. WTI peaked near US$128/bbl on April 2 before the temporary ceasefire agreed April 8 and the full Strait reopening announced April 17 sent the contract collapsing approximately 34% from that peak to US$83.8540. The 12-month average sits at US$98.15/bbl, leaving the current level 14.6% below its trailing-year average14. If WTI holds below the ninety-dollar threshold, the database's 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) would face compressed producer netbacks, with the WCS differential having widened to US$16.25/bbl below WTI on April 1341. The 52-week range runs from US$58.70/bbl to US$117.63/bbl14.

commodities.name: Western Canadian Select
commodities.commentary: Western Canadian Select: ~US$86.75/bbl (estimated, Apr 13) — the WCS discount widened to US$16.25/bbl below WTI on April 13, up from US$15.55 on April 11, reflecting pipeline capacity constraints and heavier sour crude pricing amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption41. With the April 17 WTI collapse to US$83.85, the implied WCS level dropped to approximately US$67.60, the lowest estimated heavy crude price since late 20244140. The widening differential affects netbacks for heavy crude producers across the 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) in the database41.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.commentary: Brent Crude: US$90.38/bbl (-9.0% on the April 17 session) — Brent dropped sharply on the Strait of Hormuz reopening, falling from its 52-week high of US$118.35 set during the crisis peak1540. The contract remains 47% above its year-ago level and 29.3% above its 12-month average of US$69.8715.

commodities.name: Natural Gas (Henry Hub)
commodities.commentary: Natural Gas (Henry Hub): US$2.67/MMBtu (-4.57% week-over-week) — Henry Hub fell to its lowest level since November 2024, driven by an EIA storage build of 59 Bcf for the week of April 10, exceeding forecasts, and continued mild shoulder-season demand18. The contract sits 29.98% below its year-ago level and at the floor of its 52-week range of US$2.67 to US$7.46/MMBtu18. The 12-month average is US$3.50/MMBtu, leaving the current level 23.7% below its trailing-year average. If Henry Hub holds near current levels, the 785 power and energy projects in the database tracking gas-fired generation and LNG export feedstock would carry input costs at the bottom of the observed range over the past year18.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.commentary: Gold: US$4,728/oz (+2.82% week-over-week) — gold advanced on safe-haven demand driven by the Strait of Hormuz crisis and broad US dollar depreciation, trading between US$4,656 (April 7) and US$4,816 (April 16)17. The intra-period high of US$4,816 on April 16 marked a new 52-week peak, with the metal up approximately 50% year-over-year17. The Lagging Indicator cross-reference engine links the gold move to 364 mining projects ($159.5B) in the database, where gold-linked operations carry direct revenue exposure to spot pricing17.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.commentary: Silver: US$78–80/oz range (+3.74% week-over-week) — silver tracked gold higher on safe-haven and industrial demand, climbing above US$80/oz on April 1622. The metal sits 148.84% above its year-ago level, the largest percentage year-over-year gain among the 13 commodities tracked, with the 52-week range running from US$30.32/oz to US$115.08/oz22.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.commentary: Copper: US$6.07/lb (+3.32% week-over-week) — COMEX copper advanced on a combination of AI data-center power demand, US-Iran diplomacy optimism, and China's Q1 GDP beat of 5.0% with industrial production up 6.1% year-over-year1932. The contract is up approximately 30% year-over-year and 4.91% month-over-month, the highest reading since the March 30 indicators print of US$5.53/lb19. The cross-reference engine links copper to 785 power and energy projects in the database, where the metal carries through to grid build-out and electrification cost lines19.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.commentary: Lumber: US$490/Mbf (W-SPF 2x4, +1.0% week-over-week) — NRCan reported the benchmark at US$490/Mbf for the week of April 3, up US$5 on the week, as spring building season demand offset the drag from housing starts falling 6.0% month-over-month to 235,852 SAAR in March235. The database tracks 13 forestry projects and 211 residential projects ($44.4B) with exposure to lumber as a construction input23.

commodities.name: Wheat
commodities.commentary: Wheat: US$601.75/bu (+4.7% week-over-week) — CBOT wheat advanced on global supply concerns linked to the Middle East disruption and Black Sea transport risk, up 10.7% month-over-month and 10.4% year-over-year48. The advance from the March 10 level of US$545.25/bu represents a 10.4% gain over five weeks48.

commodities.name: Uranium
commodities.commentary: Uranium: US$86.30/lb (-0.23% month-over-month) — spot uranium held near the US$86 level on April 16, up 32.67% year-over-year, reflecting sustained utility contracting demand and geopolitical supply-route concerns through the Strait of Hormuz period20. Saskatchewan-based producers Cameco (McArthur River, Cigar Lake) anchor the North American uranium production base tracked in the database's mining project count20.

commodities.name: Nickel
commodities.commentary: Nickel: US$17,985/tonne (+4.81% month-over-month) — LME nickel advanced on battery supply-chain restocking and China's industrial production gain of 6.1% year-over-year in Q1, up 14.23% year-over-year2132. The metal carries exposure to Canadian battery-metals supply-chain projects in Ontario and Quebec21.

commodities.name: Canola
commodities.commentary: Canola: CAD$726.60/tonne (May futures, April 7) — ICE canola futures held near the CAD$727 level, supported by Middle East energy disruptions lifting vegetable oil markets and tightening canola crush margins48. Prairie oilseed producers carried through to the database's 4 agriculture projects tracked in the pipeline48.

commodities.name: Potash (Nutrien proxy)
commodities.commentary: Potash (Nutrien proxy): CAD$70.19/share (-3.56% week-over-week) — Nutrien declined as fertilizer-linked names rotated lower amid the broader risk-off period, falling 4.35% month-over-month but remaining 50.34% above its year-ago level14. The 52-week range runs from CAD$48.32 to CAD$83.94, with the 12-month average at CAD$61.7914. Saskatchewan potash operations under Nutrien and Mosaic anchor the database's fertilizer-linked mining exposure14.
